films.title: REAL LIFE SUCKS
films.description: Toy Machine's tenth full-length video is a tightly edited 24-minute team film directed by Don Luong. Jeremy Leabres, Georgia Martin, Myles Willard, Axel Cruysberghs, Shiloh Catori and Braden Hoban receive the principal billing, while nine additional team riders appear across the two montages and supporting sections.
creditNotes: Toy Machine's upload explicitly bills the six principal skaters and Don Luong as director and editor.

SkateVideoSite's section-by-section catalog expands the first-party 'rest of the team' note to the complete 15-skater appearance roster; the additional nine are retained as team/montage appearances, not promoted to full-part billing.
films.historicalContext: Released as Toy Machine skateboard video number ten, REAL LIFE SUCKS is a modern company full-length rather than a trailer, episode or compilation.
films.artworkNotes: The official 480x360 YouTube thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-15. It is a genuine skate frame from the exact film; this upload has no max-resolution YouTube thumbnail, so the working hqdefault asset is retained.

films.title: Transcend 5
films.description: Eric Ferguson's fifth Transcend film is a 78-minute Salt Lake City scene document assembled from footage filmed between April 2022 and February 2025. Twenty-one skaters receive named sections or shared-part billing, while two large homies montages preserve another 39 explicitly credited appearances from the wider crew.
creditNotes: The official chapter list supplies the 21 named-section/shared-part riders and separately labels the two homies montages; all 39 montage names are preserved without upgrading them to principal-part status.
The first-party description credits Eric Ferguson for filming and editing, 13 additional filmers, Coltyn Nelson for analog photos and Dago Moncada for digital photos.
films.locationNote: Skate Jawn identifies Salt Lake City as the crew's home and explicitly lists Phoenix, Denver, Seattle, Las Vegas, Boise and Southern California as additional filming regions.
films.historicalContext: The fifth full-length in the Transcend crew series documents a multigenerational Salt Lake City street scene over nearly three years of filming.
premiereNotes: The filmmaker's description documents a March 30, 2025 premiere at the Downtown Salt Lake City Library Auditorium; the complete film was published online April 18, 2025.
films.artworkNotes: The official 1920x1080 YouTube thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-15. It carries the Transcend 5 title, shows the crew and bills the film as an Eric Ferguson skate film; it matches the exact authorized player.

films.title: CALICO
films.description: CALICO is a 17-minute independent full-length rooted in Lincoln, Nebraska. Filmed by Noah Appleget and edited by Appleget with Dawson ElDorado, it presents all 11 credited skaters in order of appearance and preserves a focused snapshot of the local street scene.
creditNotes: The complete order-of-appearance roster and supported filming/editing credits are identical in the filmmaker upload and independent SkateVideoSite catalog.
films.historicalContext: A locally produced scene full-length, CALICO documents Lincoln's independent street-skate community rather than presenting isolated parts or a compilation.
films.artworkNotes: The official 1920x1080 YouTube thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-15. It shows a skate frame at a Lincoln spot with dedicated CALICO title artwork and matches the exact filmmaker player.
